sections.notes: Use a dark theme hero with white/light text. Split layout: text block left, media/gallery block right. Primary CTA is dominant and repeated once in hero only. Secondary CTA remains empty because input has no secondary CTA. Include compact value prop line beneath supporting copy. Reserve right side for gallery-style media panel combining video/image thumbnails relevant to generated visuals; do not introduce unsupported claims.

Visitor trusts logos most, so this becomes the dominant trust signal. Because no actual badges/customer count are provided, build a placeholder-ready logo strip component frame for client-approved logos only. Keep it immediately below hero. Add a minimal trust caption line if needed, but do not fabricate customer counts or testimonials here.

Form content is empty in input, so build a reusable lead-capture shell with headline slot, field stack slot, and CTA slot for future content binding. Since this page emphasizes inquiry over direct purchase, place form early in the page after trust. Keep the module visually simple and conversion-focused. On desktop, a left-side benefit summary can accompany the form shell if needed, but do not invent copy.

Build as a featured product block with headline, description, section CTA, and 6 feature cards. Use a 3-column grid on desktop because there are 5+ features, but keep the intro card spanning full width above the grid if needed. Card style should be simple, bordered, lightly elevated, text-led. Repeat CTA at section level. This section should clearly read as the first major product offering.

Second product block with headline, description, and 6 feature cards. No CTA is provided for this block, so keep it informational and avoid inventing one. Use the same card system as Seedream for consistency. Consider a subtle section divider or tonal shift only via spacing/background, not decorative effects.

Explicitly required by context: include a gallery section containing videos and images. Use a media grid or tabbed gallery shell with slots for video thumbnails, image previews, and optional captions. Keep the gallery subordinate to the product sections, but visually strong enough to demonstrate output quality. Do not invent specific media claims or statistics.

Use the provided five testimonials in a 3-column desktop grid, with the fifth card wrapping to a second row. Include star rating row, italic quote, bold author, and muted designation. Keep cards compact and text-focused. This section supports trust after the feature blocks.

Pricing is available, so include a pricing/quote section despite the absence of full price data for one plan. Use two centered cards, one for each product, with includes checklists and CTA buttons. Preserve the provided price text exactly for Seedance 1.5 Pro. For Seedream 4.5, leave price empty but maintain quote-request structure. Keep the module inquiry-led rather than comparison-led.

Use a minimal utility footer only. Do not add unsupported navigation density. If cart artifact appears in extras, ignore it as a visible page section unless a client later requests commerce UI. Footer should be restrained and brand-consistent.

On mobile, stack media above text or keep text-only if the media gallery becomes too dense; however, because gallery is requested, use a compact media block above the copy with 1-2 swipeable previews. Primary CTA full-width. No secondary CTA. Keep headline size controlled to fit the long headline within mobile width.

Keep logo trust as an immediately visible, compact element below hero. Use horizontal scrolling or wrapped rows depending on logo count. Do not fabricate logo names in the build plan; create a reusable slot for approved partner/customer logos.
Use a full-width mobile form card. Fields stack vertically. CTA full-width and placed first in button order only after fields. Keep the form compact and accessible, with minimal chrome.

Convert the desktop feature grid into a single-column stacked card list. Maintain the same order of features. Keep the section CTA as a full-width button if displayed. Use compact card spacing and avoid dense paragraphs.
Single-column stacked cards for all Seedance features. No CTA provided. Keep section length manageable with consistent card sizing and concise spacing.
Create a mobile-first swipe gallery with video/image cards. Keep captions short or optional. This should feel like a compact proof-of-output section rather than a full portfolio grid.

Render testimonials as a vertical stack of cards. Preserve star rating row and quote formatting. Keep card height consistent and avoid dense multi-line overflow. This section can be scrollable if needed but should remain a single column.

Stack pricing cards vertically, each full width. Keep checklist items concise. Make the CTA full-width. Retain the provided Seedance starting price text exactly; keep Seedream as quote-only/blank-price as provided.
Minimal mobile footer only. Keep spacing tight and avoid unnecessary columns. Use a simple legal/help utility pattern if content is later supplied.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro to produce high-fidelity visuals, edits, and synchronized video content with professional control.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed cinematic hero with the headline anchored on the left and an immersive gallery collage occupying the right and lower depth plane, instead of a standard split layout. The background should stay dark charcoal with orange mesh glows, subtle noise, and grid lines to feel like a premium AI production studio. Make the hero feel proof-led by placing a visible logo marquee directly beneath the headline and layering three staggered output frames: a poster-style image, an ad creative, and a motion thumbnail. CTA should be a bold rounded orange button with a secondary ghost action omitted. Keep typography dramatic with a 60px+ H1, tight leading, and premium spacing for a high-confidence creative audience.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is full-bleed cinematic and visual-first, while trust is a compact marquee strip.
How-it-works uses a clean step flow instead of another gallery/card wall.
Proof uses a logo wall to create a different rhythm from the product spotlight sections.
Product sections alternate between spotlight-plus-grid and split-panel presentation to avoid visual sameness.
Testimonials shift into a carousel to break the grid cadence before the final CTA.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create professional AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Generate high-quality visuals, cinematic motion, and synchronized audio-visual content for creative teams.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark cinematic overlay with floating orb accents and layered product previews
sections.designNote: Make the hero visual-first and premium. Headline must answer what it is: AI image and video generation. Subheadline must clarify it is for creative directors, producers, art directors, marketing managers, and creative leads. Use the original CTA text exactly as the single CTA: 'Get started'. Add a compact value strip beneath the CTA with 3 micro-benefits, but keep the ad-message continuity strong.

Place trust immediately after the hero using a prominent logo marquee. Since logos are the required proof type and the audience is warm, keep this early and highly visible. If fewer than 3 usable logos are available, replace with a metric strip; otherwise prioritize 3-6 recognizable logos in a continuous band.

Use a 3-step, under-60-seconds explanation: 1) write a prompt or upload inputs, 2) choose image or video generation mode, 3) export high-quality assets. Keep this section bright and editorial to break the dark hero/trust sequence. No dense feature dump here; make it easy and fast.

Treat proof as a logo-first credibility wall, not testimonials. Use recognizable brand logos in a strong horizontal marquee or compact logo grid. This should feel authoritative and industry-relevant for creative production teams, reinforcing premium confidence before the deeper feature explanation.

Show the two product blocks as alternating premium spotlights, not a generic list. First block should focus on Seedream 4.5 with a large preview panel and a compact grid of its strongest capabilities: text-image alignment, high-resolution output, typographic rendering, multi-image composition, and structural fidelity. Second block should switch to a split-panel rhythm for Seedance 1.5 Pro, emphasizing text-to-video, audio-visual sync, multilingual lip-sync, cinematic camera control, and 10x faster inference. Keep only the 1-2 click-driving features visually dominant in each block.

Use pricing as an inquiry-oriented conversion card rather than a comparison table. Keep it simple and low-friction, with the Seedream and Seedance offer cards visually separated but aligned to one clear CTA behavior. Use the exact CTA label 'Get started' on the button and keep it solid accent color at 100% opacity.

Use a carousel because there are 4+ testimonials. Prioritize quotes from creative director, video producer, art director, and marketing manager roles to match the target audience. Keep it concise and proof-led, with one testimonial visually spotlighted at a time to reduce density after the pricing section.

End with a strong conversion card that reuses the single CTA label 'Get started'. Keep the form minimal and focused on action, not friction. Since the traffic is warm, this should feel like a direct 'see it in action' finish, not a long qualification form.
If a footer-like utility band is needed, keep it minimal and brand-clean. This area should not compete with the final CTA; it should only support wayfinding, legal, and optional secondary utility.

blueprint.designPersonality: A premium creative AI studio: dark, immersive, precise, and proof-led. It should feel like a high-end production suite for teams that care about quality, control, and brand-safe visual output.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a cinematic dark gallery layout with large JPEG hero art, stacked preview frames, and a dedicated gallery section containing both image outputs and video thumbnails. Show floating mockups of generated posters, ad creatives, and motion frames. Use SVG icons for capability badges and proof markers. Make logos the most visible trust layer through a marquee band and logo wall near the top.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so the hero needs a smaller, dense premium size to preserve balance and avoid awkward wrapping.

colours.colourReason: Brand data only provides orange, white, near-black, and light grey, so the visual identity is built around a dark charcoal base with the brand orange as the primary action and emphasis color. This keeps the page premium, high-contrast, and distinct without introducing unsupported palette choices.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Split hero with strong headline block, short supporting copy, and compact checklist-style value props; primary visual emphasis over dense explanation.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Top hero, then a lead-capture/form block, then stacked content sections with clear hierarchy and repeated feature groups.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple bordered or lightly elevated content cards with concise titles, short descriptions, and utility-first layout; no decorative glass treatment implied.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Single dominant primary CTA in the hero, repeated section-level CTA for the first product block, and low-friction conversion emphasis over multiple competing actions.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module present; layout favors inquiry/demo lead capture instead of tier comparison.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not shown in the provided markup; infer a minimal utility footer if needed, but no visual pattern is available.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Light media usage in hero/logo area and icon-assisted list items; primarily text-led sections rather than image-heavy panels.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Sequential feature sections with a headline, short explanatory paragraph, then a list of capability bullets; supports progressive disclosure of technical depth.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated form card immediately after hero, visually separated as a conversion module with hidden tracking fields and a prominent section heading.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Carousel-based hero rotation is implied; otherwise interaction is static and form-led.
designNotes: Use concise, enterprise-oriented messaging with strong hierarchy.
Favor a direct conversion path: hero CTA to form.
Keep feature sections text-dense but scannable with short bullets.
Use clear section boundaries and moderate whitespace for readability.
If adapting to a modern landing page, preserve the split hero and sequential feature storytelling without adding unnecessary ornamentation.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page should be designed as a high-intent lead-generation experience for solution-aware creative professionals. The strongest trust signal is logos, so brand proof should be elevated early and visually dominant. Because the product is about generative output quality, the hero should feel product-led and immersive, but still use a split layout to balance messaging and media. A dark theme supports the premium AI positioning and helps image/video galleries stand out. The page should move quickly from promise to proof to product detail, with concise sections, repeated demo-oriented CTAs, and a gallery that demonstrates both Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro in action.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
